name_reason: Follows the fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention; '28' is the chapter ID (valid 01-30, confirmed as index 28 in data_fd2_chapter_end_handler_table via the xref at 0x51e55), not an address residue. 'end' correctly distinguishes the chapter-end handler from the init/post-action handlers.
purpose: Chapter 28 end handler: the simplest end handler -- shows post-battle dialog page 7, persists the runtime roster, and advances to the next chapter.
logic_summary: Stack-probe (__CHK 0x28), then fd2_display_dialog_scene(data_fd2_current_chapter_text, page=7, dialog_id=0xA0000, w=0x140, h=0xCD, x=0x4C, y=0x4A, 0x13, 1), then fd2_save_runtime_char_to_template(), then data_fd2_chapter_current_chapter_id++. At the binary level the body pushes the 8 dialog args and JMPs to 0x231DF (fd2_chapter_04_end's shared epilogue tail) which pushes the chapter-text ptr, calls the dialog scene, saves the template, and increments the chapter id; the C source reconstructs this as the equivalent inline 3-statement sequence. No char recruited, no cutscene event, no branch.

returns.semantics: No return value; side effects only (dialog display, template save, current_chapter_id increment).

comment_original_issue: Content was accurate but used non-ASCII em-dash characters ('--' style was needed per the project's code-comment ASCII rule).
notes: xref source 0x51e55 confirmed as data_fd2_chapter_end_handler_table[28] (read_memory @ 0x51e51: ...64 54 02 00... = LE 0x00025464). No direct callers, as the existing comment states. The in_stack_* vars in the decompile are __CHK stack-probe artifacts, not real parameters, so params=[]. Ghidra plate is consistent with the refined src comment (plate has slightly more low-level arg-push/JMP detail; no contradiction) so plate left unchanged. Comment refinement was punctuation-only (em-dash -> '--') plus reflow; content unchanged. No game logic touched.
